claims.claim: Reviewers describe running constantly low on resources such as ammunition and health items while navigating tight police station corridors.

citations.review_text:
Literally one of the worst games I've ever played. It's extremely frustrating from start to finish. You're constantly going around in circles, struggling to find anything useful. Ammo is always running out, resources are scarce, and if you accidentally leave an important key item behind, you're basically stuck and can't progress.

You're constantly running low on both ammo and health, and the game doesn't seem to care or make any effort to help you out. No hints, no guidance, nothing. The story barely moves forward, and instead of feeling like you're making progress, it just becomes an endless grind.

I honestly can't remember the last time a game frustrated me this much. I absolutely hated it.

[h1]Survival Horror at Its Absolute Best.[/h1]

Few games manage to create an atmosphere as terrifying and immersive as Resident Evil 2.

[b]From the moment you step into Raccoon City, the tension never lets up.[/b] The environments are beautifully crafted, the sound design is phenomenal, and every dark hallway makes you think twice before taking another step.

[b]The survival mechanics are what make this experience so rewarding.[/b] Managing ammunition, conserving resources, solving puzzles, and deciding whether to fight or run creates a constant sense of vulnerability. You're never quite as comfortable as you think you are.

The level design, enemy encounters, and overall presentation are fantastic. Every area feels carefully designed, and the different character campaigns provide plenty of reasons to experience the nightmare more than once.

And then there's Mr. X. Few enemies create that level of constant anxiety simply by existing. Hearing those footsteps getting closer is an experience I'll never forget.

[b]Resident Evil 2 is a perfect example of how to modernize a classic without losing what made it special.[/b]

[h2]Welcome to Raccoon City. Hope you brought enough ammo. 🧟[/h2]

[b]An absolute masterpiece of survival horror. Highly recommended![/b]

Resident Evil 2 Remake — 88/100. An exceptional buy for $12.

The guns felt great, and every upgrade made a noticeable difference. Some of the tensest moments came when I was down to my last few bullets or had already burned through my healing items. The tight corridors of the police station made that feeling even better. Exploring them by flashlight looked amazing, and by the time I reached the sewers, I appreciated having a bit more room to move.

Leon’s first run was my favourite for discovery. Going into the station blind and slowly learning my way around was a huge part of the fun. I preferred Claire’s story, but I wish her run had given me just as much to discover. Revisiting some areas felt tedious the second time through. Claire easily had the better finale, though. Leon’s Mr. X fight felt like three minutes of dodging him and wondering whether my shots even mattered. Give me Claire’s minigun and that train sequence any day.

The sound and music helped build the atmosphere, especially in the darker areas, but I wanted a soundtrack I’d still be thinking about afterwards. A few dead zombies ragdolled in ways that took me out of the moment. Otherwise, the game ran extremely well.

I’d love to forget the layout of that police station and experience it all over again. For the $12 I paid, this was an exceptional buy. It’s left me wanting more, and I’ve got the whole franchise ahead of me.

Overall: Solid Game

Pros: Great survival gameplay, I love running around tight corridors and managing my resources. Deciding if I should unload on some zombies to clear out an area so I don't take damage in the future at the expense of wasting ammo. Making decisions like that is what I found most fun about the game.

Cons: I don't like the "realistic momentum" movement in the game, I prefer the snappyness of the originals, it allows for quicker and tighter gameplay. Also not a fan of the combat, especially the bosses.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe multiple playthrough campaigns as feeling repetitive because the scenarios share the same maps, puzzles, and bosses with little variation.

citations.review_text:
This game was very enjoyable. I played RE4+5+6 before this one and compared to RE6 this game was pretty chill. A lot of running around and puzzeling. What I didn't understand was the concept of 4 scenarios. For me they all felt the same. Same puzzles, same enemies, almost same maps and bosses. Felt like a repetetive waste of time, but overall the game is good.

[h3]STORY [SPOILERS][/h3]
You can play 4 scenarios. There's A and B for Leon S. Kennedy and A and B vor Claire Redfield. As mentioned above, they can feel repetetive. You start at RPD, then you leave RPD, then you enter the sewers, then you find the underground laboratory, then you fight the endboss. Game ends.

[h3]CHARACTERS[/h3]
[u]Leon Kennedy[/u]
The rookie on his first day. I love the fact that his actor actually speaked in a higher voice, knowing that this Leon version is young and unexperienced. 
[u]Claire Redfield[/u]
The sister of Chris Redfield. I never met Claire in any games before, so this was my first time playing her and getting to know her character and personality. She's a tough but caring woman. Her interaction with Sherry (the girl she saves) is a little bit weird sometimes, like: "Your dad died? Mine too! At least we have something in common!" - girl, what? 
[u]Sherry Birkin[/u]
The daughter of the mad scientist William Birkin. You can play Sherry while she's in the orphanage. Otherwise she follows Claire around.
[u]Ada Wong[/u]
The spy. She meets Leon and they start working together. I like her design, she is SO pretty and (compared to RE4R) her voice actress actually gave her somewhat of a personality.
[u]Mister X[/u] and [u]Birkin[/u]
Mister X will hunt you down in the RPD and will probably give you some nice jumpscares. Birkin will be your enemy down in the underground laboratory. 

[h3]GAMEPLAY[/h3]
As mentioned above, I played RE6 before RE2R and this game felt so chill compared to the action-heavy RE6. Just running around in the RPD, everything is quiet except some zombies or the f…

7/10

They succeed with the claustrophobic horror and the puzzles. The narrative developed nicely throughout the game. A remake that kept the core, polished and added things without loosing touch of the original.

I dislike "you have to play the game twice" to see the full story. I think its a way of trying to fool gamers that the game is longer than it is. I guess the "run around the same level over and over" is part of this classics charm with the puzzles, but still its a bit filler but I can see past that.

This game marks the beginning of Resident Evil's golden boy, Leon Kennedy. Although he is overused nowadays, it's really interesting to see his first appearance and watch how he develops over the course of the story. Overall, the game is a lot of fun, and the DLC was pretty good too. The 100% drags out a bit because you have to complete Claire A/B and Leon A/B—which I did—and they don't change enough, making it feel repetitive.

Game: 7/10

100%: 5/10

claims.claim: Reviewers note that completing multiple campaigns across Leon and Claire leads to repetitive playthroughs with similar maps, bosses, and puzzles.

citations.review_text:
This game was very enjoyable. I played RE4+5+6 before this one and compared to RE6 this game was pretty chill. A lot of running around and puzzeling. What I didn't understand was the concept of 4 scenarios. For me they all felt the same. Same puzzles, same enemies, almost same maps and bosses. Felt like a repetetive waste of time, but overall the game is good.

[h3]STORY [SPOILERS][/h3]
You can play 4 scenarios. There's A and B for Leon S. Kennedy and A and B vor Claire Redfield. As mentioned above, they can feel repetetive. You start at RPD, then you leave RPD, then you enter the sewers, then you find the underground laboratory, then you fight the endboss. Game ends.

[h3]CHARACTERS[/h3]
[u]Leon Kennedy[/u]
The rookie on his first day. I love the fact that his actor actually speaked in a higher voice, knowing that this Leon version is young and unexperienced. 
[u]Claire Redfield[/u]
The sister of Chris Redfield. I never met Claire in any games before, so this was my first time playing her and getting to know her character and personality. She's a tough but caring woman. Her interaction with Sherry (the girl she saves) is a little bit weird sometimes, like: "Your dad died? Mine too! At least we have something in common!" - girl, what? 
[u]Sherry Birkin[/u]
The daughter of the mad scientist William Birkin. You can play Sherry while she's in the orphanage. Otherwise she follows Claire around.
[u]Ada Wong[/u]
The spy. She meets Leon and they start working together. I like her design, she is SO pretty and (compared to RE4R) her voice actress actually gave her somewhat of a personality.
[u]Mister X[/u] and [u]Birkin[/u]
Mister X will hunt you down in the RPD and will probably give you some nice jumpscares. Birkin will be your enemy down in the underground laboratory. 

[h3]GAMEPLAY[/h3]
As mentioned above, I played RE6 before RE2R and this game felt so chill compared to the action-heavy RE6. Just running around in the RPD, everything is quiet except some zombies or the f…

Nice game. Hoped that Claire run would be quite different, but is almost the same. Could have had more (different) bosses: in both runs MF Burking always comes back and Mr. X was mogged in Claire run. The shock gun is horrible!

This game marks the beginning of Resident Evil's golden boy, Leon Kennedy. Although he is overused nowadays, it's really interesting to see his first appearance and watch how he develops over the course of the story. Overall, the game is a lot of fun, and the DLC was pretty good too. The 100% drags out a bit because you have to complete Claire A/B and Leon A/B—which I did—and they don't change enough, making it feel repetitive.

Game: 7/10

100%: 5/10

claims.claim: Reviewers note that ammo conservation, careful resource management, and strategic shooting are necessary to survive encounters.

citations.review_text:
Well, after nearly 30 hours, I have finished the main story, playing as Leon first and Claire second. It's really hard to say anything new about the game. The huge number of overwhelmingly positive reviews says it all.

Both the graphics and gameplay are great. The flashlight and those wonderful shadows create an incredible atmosphere. I remember how difficult the old Resident Evil games were, mostly because of the camera angles and the very limited inventory. The good news is that the camera issues are gone and the inventory can be expanded. Still, that doesn't make the game a cakewalk. A keen eye, ammo conservation and careful shooting are necessary if you want to avoid seeing the loading screen. Finishing the campaign doesn't mean the fun is over. There are some additional modes focused on beating time records and, of course, the hard mode, where you'll meet your old friend – the ink ribbon.

Overall, the Resident Evil 2 Remake is one of the best zombie games I have played. It combines the best elements of the original PSX game with modern solutions and improvements. The same story combined with new gameplay mechanics works wonders. I'm sure I'll visit Raccoon City many times in the future.

Get this game. If you are a resident evil fan, especially 4, you will love this...though with a cavet, it still harkens to the old style of resident evil of picking your fights, rationing ammo and memorizing the map to remember routes.

But man, this was a good ride through and through to grab all the achievements. Hard yes, but worth it.

Resident Evil 2 (Remake) 

​Stunning RE Engine Visuals: Phenomenal graphics, realistic gore, and top-tier lighting that masterfully create a horrifying atmosphere.
​Masterclass Puzzle Design: Brilliant and satisfying brain-teasers that reward careful exploration of every corner.
​Incredible Horror Atmosphere: Immersive, tense environment where every sound and shadow keeps you strictly on edge.
​Scarcity of Ammo & Weapons: Resource mechanics heavily limit your arsenal and available ammo, creating stress that isn't for everyone.
​Lack of Interactive Cinematic Events: Story presentation relies heavily on pre-rendered cutscenes rather than dynamic, player-driven scripted events.
​Narrow Scope of Survivors: Story feels isolated; missed opportunities regarding citywide chaos, hospital hunts, or encountering diverse survivor groups.
​Monotonous Nighttime Setting: Entirely locked within a single dark night across limited, claustrophobic indoor locations.
​Relentless Enemies: Zombie durability can sometimes cross the line into feeling tedious rather than genuinely scary.
​The Good: Peak survival horror experience boasting elite visuals, stellar exploration, and iconic level design!
​The Verdict: A absolute masterpiece of puzzle-horror, slightly held back by restricted scale, low ammo pools, and environmental repetition. 8.5/10.

Resident Evil 2 Remake is genuinely an amazing game. The atmosphere is incredible, the gameplay feels smooth, and the attention to detail is impressive. Exploring the RPD, solving puzzles, managing resources, and trying to survive every encounter make the experience really enjoyable.

The horror elements are done perfectly, especially whenever Mr. X shows up. The tension he creates makes every moment feel unpredictable. I also loved playing as both Leon and Claire, as their stories make the experience even better.

Overall, it's a perfect combination of survival horror, action, and exploration. Definitely one of the best remakes I've played and a must-play for anyone who enjoys good games.

single_points.text: One reviewer says playing with headphones unlocks incredible 3D audio that lets you clearly hear enemies moving around you and track which floor Mr X is on.

citation.review_text:
Resident Evil 2 Remake is an absolute masterpiece and one of the best remakes ever made. The game captures everything that made the original special while elevating it with modern presentation and tighter design. Sound design stands out as truly exceptional. Playing with headphones unlocks incredible 3D audio that makes the experience fully immersive. You can clearly hear enemies moving around you, and Mr X’s heavy stomping through the RPD is especially effective. The audio cues let you track which floor he is on, turning tension into something tactical and unforgettable. Characters and enemies look excellent with strong design work and smooth animations. The ability to shoot limbs off zombies to slow them down feels satisfying and adds a useful layer of combat strategy. Mr X himself is pure nightmare fuel. He relentlessly chases you through the RPD and creates constant anxiety, especially when you are trying to solve puzzles or complete objectives. You have to work quickly, then either run or find ways to slow him down. Running near him or the Lickers will alert them, so careful walking or direct confrontation becomes necessary. There is plenty of content to unlock afterward, including costumes and extra modes that extend the replay value significantly. One important tip: play the DirectX 11 version. You can access it through Steam by going to the game properties, betas tab, and selecting the dx11 option. The default DirectX 12 version that ships with the game enables ray tracing, but the performance is far worse than the DX11 build.
Overall this is an outstanding remake that every survival horror fan should play.

★★★★★
